item.title: Lost walker, near Sittaford Tor
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
January 27, 2022

Callout #3

The Police called DSRT Tavistock at 13:39 to request us to assist a walker lost on the Moor who had become separated from her husband, who had the map and compass.. Use of SARLOC gave us the  location of the subject and after discussion with colleagues in DSRT Okehampton it was agreed that we would send in a hill party from Postbridge and they would send in a team via Fernworthy Forest.  Our members located the lady and walked her north to meet transport at Fernworthy Forest, while her husband was escorted in his car to Fernworthy to be reunited with her.

item.title: Injured Walker, Great Staple Tor
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
January 08, 2022

Callout #2

At 12:16  the Police called Dartmoor Search & Rescue Team (Tavistock) to rescue a female walker with a broken ankle on Great Staple Tor.  The team was deployed with Land Rover '63', and a Sarloc text sent to the casualty party to double-check their grid reference.  

The Air Ambulance was also tasked but the stretcher party continued as the helicopter was unlikely to be able to land very close to the casualty-site, if at all in the conditions of strong winds and driving rain.  Once the helimed paramedics had treated the casualty the team packaged her up in a vacuum mattress and casualty-bag and transferred her by stretcher to the helicopter.  

The remaining members of the party, a Ten Tors team in training with their adult leaders, were walked back to the RV and their waiting minibus.  They thanked us for our speedy response, surprised to see the first team members coming over the hill only 30 minutes after calling 999.  Everyone was off the hill by 1400, at which point the rain stopped!

item.title: Missing person, Bickleigh
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Two days of searching for the team alongside other DRG teams and police and Fire search teams

Callout 4 - 11th February

We were called to assist Dartmoor Search and Rescue Team - Plymouth in a search for a missing male who was deemed to be at high risk. Extensive searches were carried out in dense woodland and and also beneath the viaducts. Active search deployments were suspended at around midnight.

Callout 5 - 12th February

We resumed the search, joined again by members of DSRT’s Plymouth and Ashburton and later by East Cornwall SRT. Multiple searches were carried out over a more extensive area, but the male was not found.

We have since been told the missing male has been located, safe and well.

item.title: Storm Eunice
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded: We, along with many of the Search and Rescue teams in the region, were on standby in readiness for Storm Eunice. Members of the Team met at the Rescue Centre at 05:00 ready to assist when tasked by the police. Fortunately the team only tasked with "structurally dangerous" jobs as no flooding or medical incidents required the team.

item.title: Injured lady walker, south of Wistman‘s Wood
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: 13th March At 14:00 DSRT Tavistock was called to assist a 72year old lady who had fallen and suffered a painful injury to her shoulder. Because of the pain she was unable to walk well and had become extremely cold. Our advance party located her on the track just south of Crockern Cottage, administered analgesia and got her into a Team LandRover. While she was warming a splint was applied to immobilise and support her arm and she was then driven down the track to the Two Bridges Hotel, where the family car was parked. She was handed over to the care of family members to transport her to Derriford Hospital, as no SWAST ambulances were available, due to high call numbers.

item.title: 28/03/2022 Major Incident near Mary Tavy
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Callout 8 A major incident was declared at 18:50 because of a large wild fire on the moor, just north of Mary Tavy on the east side of the A386. Initially the fire was moving in the direction of the village and DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 19:05 to assist in the evacuation of properties at risk. A few minutes after arrival at the RV point we were advised that the fire was now moving away from Mary Tavy and evacuation of properties was no longer anticipated and we were stood down.

item.title: 14/04/2022 High Risk Missing Male
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Callout 9 DSRT Tavistock was called in the early evening by our colleagues in DSRT Plymouth to assist them in a Police search based in Leigham, for a 61 year old male deemed to be at high risk. The subject had been missing from his home address for 24 hours. Our Teams searched areas of woodland and dense undergrowth for several hours, assisted by members of Devon & Somerset Fire and Rescue Service and a helicopter from the National Police Air Service. As final deployments of the night were beginning we were informed that the subject had been located out of our search areas, near Cadover Bridge, and we were stood down at 21:30.

item.title: 18/04/2022 Missing High Risk Teenager
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 10. The Police called at 20:00 to request our assistance in a search for a teenage female, believed to be at high risk. She had been missing since mid afternoon and a message suggested she was in woodland in the Walkham valley between Horrabridge and Gem Bridge. Police officers and a helicopter from the National Police Air Service had already begun the search. On arrival at the RV point at Bedford Bridge car park, as darkness fell, our first deployment was to the far side of Gem Bridge and another was along the cycleway on the old railway line. Information from the helicopter indicated that the subject was below Gem Bridge. Police officers made first contact and then she was examined by one of our members, a paramedic. Fortunately her injuries were not serious and she was transported back to the RVP in a Team LandRover. A good outcome from inter-agency working.

item.title: 8/05/2022 Injured male in Tavy Cleave
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 11 At around 12:30 the Police requested our assistance with an incident in Tavy Cleave. A 25 year old male had fallen when trying to jump across the leat, and sustained a suspected fracture to his lower leg or ankle. Our response teams were able to reach him quickly as several of our hill parties were close by, monitoring the teams taking part in the Army Ten Tors event. He was assessed and analgesia administered before his leg was immobilised with a vacuum splint. He was then stretchered along the narrow, rough path alongside the leat to be transferred to an Ambulance at Lanehead. The Ambulance then tranported him to hospital, while our members returned to providing safety cover for Ten Tors.

item.title: 15/05/2022 Injured Cyclist, Gawton
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 12. We were called by the Police at 1500 to assist South West Ambulance Service Trust at Gawton Gravity Hub, where a mountain biker was reported to have had fallen down a 25ft drop.  Not long after the team were mobilised the Police informed us that having now assessed the scene the Ambulance crew could evacuate without our help, so at 1517 hours we stood down.  We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

item.title: 23/05/2022 18 year old with medical incident, Sheepstor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 13.At 12:34 the Police called DSRT Tavistock to assist the Ambulance service with an incident on the track below the northern slope of Sheep's Tor, by Narrator Plantation. It was reported that an 18 year old was suffering from prolonged fitting.. Team members and one of our Land Rovers were deployed but were stood down en route, as the Ambulance personnel no longer required assistance with the casualty.

item.title: 30/05/2022 Despondent female, Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 14. At 20:04 the Police requested our team to assist in the search for a female teenager deemed to be at high risk. She had been missing since 14:30 , last seen near the Community College. As team members gathered at our Rescue Centre, ready to begin a search a Police helicopter sighted her on the old railway line just west of Tavistock Hospital. Several members were deployed to bridges either side of her location and accompanied Police who took the subject into their care.

item.title: 30/06/2022 Despondent Female. Newbridge Dartmoor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 15. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 0810 to assist DSRT(Ashburton) in searching for a despondent lady in the Newbridge area.  11 members deployed with both team Land Rovers. Our water-rescue sled was used by members of our water team to search parts of the River Dart.  Other members and Search Dog Pip searched the riparian corridor and nearby woodland. 

This was a multi-agency incident attended by 3 Dartmoor SRTs, Police dog & drone teams, a Police helicopter, and Devon & Somerset Fire & Rescue water team,  with USAR, Coastguard & East Cornwall SRT arriving to relieve us as we left just before 1600 hours..

We're pleased to hear that the subject of the search was located alive this evening.

item.title: 06/07/2022 Missing male near Wotter
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 16. Around 10:00 DSRT Tavistock was called by our sister team from Plymouth to assist the Police in a search for a 36 year old male deemed to be at risk. As search teams were deploying from the search control near Beatland Corner the search was stood down, as the subject had been located out of area, in Torquay.

item.title: 9/7/2022 Injured walker between Naker's Hill and Green Hill
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 17. DSRT Tavistock was called by our sister team in Ashburton at 15:15 to assist a young lady taking part in a D of E expedition. She had sustained an ankle injury which prevented her from continuing. The group of four was sited in a remote part of the moor with no vehicular access, so members had to haul our kit across rough hilly ground to reach them. They were dehydrated, so water was given while the injury was assessed. DSRT Plymouth was called early on to assist us and four of their members joined us as we stretchered the injured girl back towards Nun's Cross Ford. From there all four young ladies were transported in a Team Land Rover to he handed over to the care of their supervisor at Peat Cot at 18:50. All members returned to the RVP by 19:00 after a tiring stretcher haul of nearly four miles in very hot conditions.

item.title: 31.5.23 Injured walker at Ger Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 11. At 18.41 the team was called by the Police to assist an injured walker. The subject had fallen about 4 metres from GerTor and suffered a deep laceration to her head and suspected rib fractures. Our advance party deployed from Lanehead as a Devon Air Ambulance approached the tor. Once the casualty had been assessed our Team members assisted the aircrew to stretcher her to the airframe and load her on board, for transfer to hospital. We wish hr a speedy recovery.

item.title: 25/07/22 Lost cyclist near White Barrow
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 18. We were called at 00:33 by Police Control to assist a lone, male cyclist who was lost on the track between White Barrow and Broad Down.

He was reported to be cold but uninjured. We deployed from the Quarry Car Park above Peter Tavy and deployed two teams in our team Landrovers along the track to White Barrow.

We also attempted two phone locations texts before we got confirmation of location. A team located the cyclist at 02:40, assessed and then escorted him back to our waiting vehicles. The police gave him, and his bike, a lift back to his accommodation in Moretonhampstead. It transpired that he was undertaking a charity cycle ride from Land's End to john O'Groats, but his navigation system had diverted him via a Dartmoor bridleway !

Vehicles were returned to the Rescue Centre by 04:30 and members were home by 05:00, on Monday morning!

item.title: 3/08/2022 Injured walker in Foggintor Quarry
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 19. DSRT Tavistock was called at 13:27 by the Police who requested us to recover an injured walker from Foggintor Quarry. The 61 year old lady had sustained a suspected fracture of her right ankle when stumbling on rough ground in the quarry. She was located within 20 minutes of the callout message and her injury assessed. After the limb had been splinted she was stretchered out of the quarry via the boggy southern exit and transferred to a Team Landrover. A SWASfT paramedic arrived and reassessed the casualty and gave further analgesia. We transported her to the public highway where the Ambulance personnel took over her care for transport to Derriford Hospital. We wish her a smooth recovery.

item.title: 7/08/2022 Missing male, Pensilva
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 20. DSRT Tavistock was called at 18:43 by our colleagues in East Cornwall SRT to assist them in a search for a male last seen at 10:50. The subject of the search was known to have some symptoms of dementia. Not long after a callout message had been sent to our members to deploy to Pensilva we were stood down as the gentleman had been located.

item.title: 25/08/22 Call out to assist Exmoor
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 21: We were called today to assist Exmoor Search & Rescue Team in a search for a despondent who went missing yesterday. Effective searching of the dense thicket-stage plantations was difficult overnight, so we were tasked to re-search them today in daylight. A team Land Rover and 6 team members deployed to near Chawleigh in mid Devon.

Shortly before 17:00 the missing person approached a member of the public, who caught the attention of the DSFRS search dog handler nearby. It's thought that hearing the dog may have prompted her to move.

We're glad that she was found alive and well, especially after being out overnight.

item.title: 18/10/22 Missing Male, Okehampton
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 22. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 0806 to continue a search for a despondent missing from Okehampton, last seen heading in the direction of Fatherford Bridge.  Given that the misper had left the previous morning this still presented a huge search area, covered with many footpaths.  Vehicle deployments and initial 'hasty' searches, including a dog team, enabled us to cover the most likely routes and sites quickly.  

With late morning came some new information so we could better focus our efforts, aided by reinforcements from DSRT(Okehampton), who had been out overnight, and another dog team.  

The missing person was located at 14:03. Our thoughts are with the family at this difficult time.

item.title: 22/10/22 Missing High Risk Male, Milton Abbot
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 23. Our team was called by the Police at 08:43 to assist in a search for a 38 year old male, who had been missing for nearly 24 hours. Information suggested that he may be at high risk. We deployed two air-scenting search dog teams along with 23 other members for an extensive search of a range of terrain, including woodland and open fields. It was a joint agency search involving Police personnel, firemen from the Urban Search and Rescue unit, Police drone teams and a helicopter from the National Police Air Service. Around lunchtime further information was received that suggested the subject may have moved out of our search area and it was agreed that our Team should suspend the search at 14:00. Some other agencies remained to continue to gather information.

item.title: 26/10/22 Injured female walker, North of Postbridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 24. The Police called out our team at 12:07 to assist the Ambulance service with a casualty on the open moor, north of Postbridge. A 15 year old female, one of a Dof E expedition training group, had slipped and fallen injuring her right hip and was unable to walk further. The location was near the East Dart River, about 500m south of the Beehive Hut. Our members deployed with a stretcher from Postbridge car park and reached her within 20 minutes. A crew from South West Ambulance Service was met at the site and following assessment she was packaged onto our stretcher and carried over open moorland, and then a tree fallen over the footpath had to be negotiated before handover at the Ambulance at 14:07. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 28/10/22 Injured Walker, Knowle Down, Walkhampton
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 25. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 16:26 to assist South West Ambulance Service with the evacuation of an injured walker. The 31 year old man had slipped over and sustained a fracture of his right ankle. Our stretcher party reached the casualty site in 30 minutes. Ambulance personnel splinted the fractured limb and administered analgesia before we stretchered the subject along a muddy track, and he was then transferred into the SWASfT Ambulance to be taken to Derriford hospital. We wish him a speedy and uneventful recovery.

item.title: 5/11/22 Collapsed Male, Walkhampton
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 26.

DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 08:29 to assist the Ambulance service to locate a 68 year old man with chest pains who had set out to cycle from Walkhampton Church to Princetown along the old railway line.  The casualty and his wife's mobile phones were called by the Police and by our Sarloc location app but no contact was achieved. A What 3 Words given by the subject to Ambulance control indicated he was about 1km NE of Walkhampton Church. A speedy response was enabled by a team member resident in Walkhampton who drove to the church and deployed from there, to be joined by a team Land Rover with oxygen, defibrillator and basic life support equipment.  The remaining team members deployed from Leedon Tor car park with duplicate kit.  Meanwhile Police officers were checking the alternative footpath and area around the Church. We were stood down at 09:18, when informed that the subject was in the care of South West Ambulance personnel, and our 17 members who had responded returned, soaking wet, to their vehicles.. Chest pains are always a high priority, and a rapid multi-agency response ended with a good outcome. We wish him a speedy recovery.

Postscript: The Team was eventually informed that, after the 999 call including the W3W detail had been made, the subject had managed to reach Walkhampton village, and that is where the Ambulance service attended to him.

item.title: 21.11.2022 Male missing in River Walkham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 27. At 22:31 DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police to provide Swift Water Rescue assistance to an incident in Horrabridge. A male had been reported to be missing in the fast-flowing river and the Fire Service was in attendance and a Police helicopter had done an air search using heat seeking equipment. As our members arrived on scene a discussion between the agencies present resulted in a decision to stand assets down, as there was doubt that any person had actually been in the water.

item.title: 24.11.22 Missing Walker, Milton Abbot
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 28. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 20:39 to assist the Police in a search for a missing walker who was staying at Hotel Endsleigh.  She and her husband had been walking back alongside the river from Horsebridge.  Her husband had been walking behind her towards the end, so was surprised to find her not back before him.  

19 team members and 3 vehicles deployed, including a search dog & handler and a swiftwater rescue team with sled.  The first team was tasked to conduct a hasty search along the riverbank path, staying in the 'cold' (safe) zone away from the swollen river's edge, whilst other search parties were readied.  About 500m from the RV they met the misper, who was well and still walking, and escorted her back to the car park.  Apparently she'd become disoriented in the woods and had only just found her way back to near the Hotel.  The Police then  took her to be reunited with her husband, so a happy ending to what turned out to be a long day!

item.title: 25.11.22 Injured Walker, King's Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 29. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 13:25 by the Ambulance service to attend a casualty on Kings Tor, who had fallen between 2 rock stacks and injured her lower leg.  16 members deployed, despite being during working hours, with all 3 vehicles despatched to ensure adequate rope rescue kit was on hand should it be needed. 

The first team went out in Land Rover '63' to assess and provide casualty care.  By the time reinforcements arrived to help extricate her and move her onto the stretcher they had splinted her leg and administered analgesia for pain relief.  A short stretcher haul to 63 followed, in which the casualty was evacuated to the RV and a waiting ambulance, accompanied by the HART Paramedic we had escorted to the casualty site.  

Both the casualty and her daughter were tending towards cold stress having been stationary and rained on since the incident occurred, even though some other walkers had very kindly lent their spare clothing.  It really shows how quickly you can get cold if you stop moving, especially if injured.

Fortuitously, our training on Wednesday had included extraction from awkward locations and a refresher on hypothermia ready for winter, which helped ensure an extra swift and efficient response.  We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

item.title: 26.12.22 Injured Dog, Burrator Reservoir Dam
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 30. At 16:19 DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at the request of Devon & Somerset Fire & Rescue Service who required assistance in a search for an injured dog. OBI, a black labrador had vaulted the parapet of Burrator Reservoir dam and fallen around 50 feet into the valley below. He was spotted by a member of the public but then disappeared. Mountain Rescue Teams do not usually search for lost animals, but to avoid risk to members of the public who were intent on searching in darkness alongside fast flowing water we deployed our members who are trained and equipped for such tasks. Within minutes of beginning our search pattern OBI was spotted and his owners were escorted to him. He was assessed by one of our members who is a veterinary surgeon and then carried to a Team LandRover for transport to a veterinary practice in Yelverton for treatment. A happy end to Boxing Day for all concerned.

item.title: 21.01.2023 Collapsed female, Tamar Trails, Gulworthy
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: 2023 Incident 1. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 12:32 to assist the Ambulance service with a collapsed female walker in woodland near Gulworthy. Two members were deployed from the RV point at Tamar Trails Car Park to establish the exact location of the casualty. On arrival at the site they were informed that the lady had been confirmed deceased. The rest of our Team members then took equipment and a wheeled stretcher to recover her down to the waiting Ambulance. She was handed back to the custody of the Ambulance crew at 13:40. Our thoughts are with her family and friends at this sad time.

item.title: 4.2.2023 Missing person.
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 2: At 00:16 the Police requested our assistance with a missing person who had failed to check out of their holiday accommodation as planned, leading to the owners reporting a concern for welfare.

Whilst one of our search managers liaised with the Police to plan the search strategy, a two person team with one of our search dogs from Mountain Rescue Search Dogs England were deployed to search the local quarries which were identified as high probability areas. The Police also launched a drone.

The dog team found the missing person, sadly deceased, shortly before 05:00.

We then used the combined efforts of our specialist water and ropes teams, along with other team members forming a stretcher party, to retrieve the person.

The whole operation took 11 hours Our thoughts and condolences go to the family and friends of the deceased at this truly difficult time

item.title: 7.2.2023 Injured Walker, Beardown Tor
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 3: We were called to assist an injured casualty with another walker near Beardown Tor.

As our first team were deploying up the track, the casualty and other walker had been met by a farmer who kindly transported the injured person to Two Bridges. One of our casualty carers checked the injury, and the rest of the team were stood down.

A positive end to a short call out We wish them a speedy recovery

item.title: 14.2.2023 Deceased male, Hart Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 4. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 14:34 to assist in the recovery of a deceased walker who had been found at Hart Tor. Ambulance personnel had confirmed death, but were unable to evacuate the gentleman over rough moorland. We deployed a stretcher party from Soldiers Pond car park and recovered him back and handed over to the care of undertakers at 16:10. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this sad time.

item.title: 1.4.2023 Casualties at Dinger Tor and Great Kneeset
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 5. At 14.30 North Dartmoor Search & Rescue Team requested our logistical support to assist them in moving personnel to two separate concurrent incidents. The teenage casualties were reported to be hypothermic. DSRT Tavistock was put on standby in case further personnel were required to assist in evacuation of the subjects. One Land Rover was deployed and used to transport a hill party to Dinger Tor and then recover them from OP15.

One casualty was transported from the moor by Land Rover and the other airlifted by a National Police Air Service helicopter, which had found a window in the very low cloud.

item.title: 8.4.2023 Injured horse rider near Hawks' Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 6. DSRT Plymouth called DSRT Tavistock at 12.23 to request our assistance with the evacuation of an injured horse rider near Hawks' Tor. The male rider had fallen from his mount and was suspected to have sustained rib fractures and was unable to walk off the moor.. Members from both Teams were deployed to the incident site to assist South West Ambulance personnel and the casualty was transported in a six-wheeled Polaris vehicle down to an Ambulance at the roadside. Members of Tavistock team assisted in transferring him into the ambulance. A successful multi-agency operation. We wish him a speedy recovery.

item.title: 12.4.2023 Injured walker north of Postbridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 7. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 12:20 to respond to a report of an injured walker located somewhere east of the East Dart waterfall, north of Postbridge. We were unable to get a fix on the casualty site using our SARLOC technology, as phone signal in that area is very poor, so on arrival at Postbridge a hill party was deployed to search upstream along the east bank of the river to locate the subject. A further team was then deployed up the west side of the river. The weather was horrendous, with gale force winds and driving torrential rain and hail. The group was spotted to the west of the river above Braddon Lake stream by the east bank team, who directed the west bank team onto the casualty site. The injured lady had slipped at 10:30 and suffered a suspected broken left ankle. A passing walker had stopped to assist and give reassurance. By the time our members reached her at 13:50 she was extremely cold so was rapidly assessed, splinted, and placed in an insulated casualty bag with heat packs. She was transported on a stretcher back to Postbridge and then transferred to a waiting SWAST Ambulance. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 23.04.2023 Injured walker near Whiteworks
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 8. DSRT Tavistock was called at 12:20 to assist a 74 year old walker who had sustained a suspected fracture of her ankle. The incident had occurred to the north of Whiteworks. We sent a SARLOC message to confirm the location. Two Team members were transported by Land Rover from the RV near Peat Cot to the end of the track by Whiteworks and quickly deployed in heavy rain to locate the casualty and provide shelter and assistance. As they neared the casualty site, within 30 minutes from the callout, they reported that a Devon Air Ambulance had already landed and confirmed that the casualty was on the opposite side of the Strane River to the aircraft. Several of our members assisted the aircrew in getting the casualty, who was already packaged on a stretcher, across the river and carried her approximately 100 metres to the helicopter. They assisted with the loading into the aircraft for evacuation to hospital. Our remaining members were stood down and all returned to the RVP by 13:40. We wish the lady an uneventful recovery from her injury, which was confirmed to be an open fracture.

item.title: 17.05.2023 Unwell walker south of Combshead Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 9. DSRT Tavistock was called at 12:59 to assist a 76 year old walker who had become unwell during a walk with a rambling group. He was unstable and nauseous and could walk no further. Although an Ordnance Survey grid reference had been given by the group when they called for assistance, that information was not passed to us, and so a search was begun by our advance hill party around Combshead Tor, which had been mentioned. The group was soon located 500m south of the Tor on the side of the valley and the gentleman assessed by one of Casualty Carers. A stretcher party was sent to the site, accompanied by two South West Ambulance personnel. The subject was then stretchered 2.5km over rough and boggy ground and then along the track back to a waiting Ambulance at Norsworthy Bridge. The rest of his group returned with our members..

item.title: 28.5.23 Teenager with medical issues near East Dart Waterfall
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 10. At 23:15 our Team was called to assist the Ambulance service in recovering a casualty from the moor. A teenage girl in a large group who were camping north of Postbridge had been taken ill with severe migraine and had suffered some minor seizures. An advance party, accompanied by two SWASfT paramedics was deployed to locate the subject and a second hill party deployed with a stretcher and full kit. The incident site was just south of the East Dart waterfall. After assessment by the paramedics the teenager was escorted down to our RVP at Postbridge, and handed over to an Ambulance crew at 02:35. A good outcome from joint agency working.

item.title: 31.5.23 Injured walker at Ger Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 11. At 18:41 our team was called to assist an injured walker. The subject had fallen 4 metres from a rock stack at Ger Tor and sustained a deep laceration to her scalp and suspected rib fractures. Our advance party deployed from Lanehead toward the tor as a Devon Air Ambulance approached. Once the subject had been assessed and treated our members assisted the aircrew to stretcher her to the airframe and load her onboard for transfer to hospital. We wish her a swift recovery.

item.title: 11.6.23 High risk missing male, Leigham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 12. DSRT Tavistock was called at 01:55 to assist our colleagues in DSRT Plymouth in a search for a 79 year old man missing from home since lunchtime the previous day, who was deemed to be at high risk. Fifteen of our members responded. Multiple searches of wooded and overgrown areas continued through the night until 08:45, when we were informed that he had been located safe and well, outside of our search areas.

item.title: 27.7.23 High risk missing male, Yelverton
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 13. The Police called DSRT Tavistock at 11:05 to search for a 55 year old male, who was deemed to be at high risk. He had been missing from his sheltered accommodation in Yelverton for over 24 hours. He was already known to us, having been the subject of separate searches carried out by us in 2019. That knowledge influenced the choice of search areas, which focussed on woodland and tracks around Burrator reservoir. We stood down at around 18:30 as our colleagues in DSRT Plymouth began searching of other areas.

item.title: 1.8.23 Lost family group, Bellever Forest
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 14. At 17:55 DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police to assist a group who had become lost during a walk in Bellever Forest. The party consisted of an 84 year old lady, her daughter, two 7 year old children and a dog. An initial search party quickly located them just outside the woodland and escorted them to the RVP at Higher Cherrybrook Bridge car park. They were then transported back to their car at the northern end of the forest. Their intended short walk had turned into more of a trek. Luckily they were returned to their car just as torrential rain began, none the worse for their extended trip.

We work hard to promote Moorland Safety, and so a gentle reminder: During this time of unseasonal weather ensure that you have suitable clothing for all that can befall you, and carry means of navigation, for example a map and compass or GPS enabled device.

item.title: 3.8.23 Injured lady, Hotel Endsleigh
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 15. At 16:44 DSRT Tavistock was requested to assist the Ambulance Service with the recovery of an injured walker from the Arboretum at Hotel Endsleigh, Milton Abbot. The 66 year old subject had sustained a suspected fractured ankle when she slipped on a steep, muddy track in the woodland. The Ambulance personnel treated the casualty and we then placed her in a casualty bag and vacuum mattress and stretchered her back to the waiting SWASfT Ambulance at the hotel. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 30.8.23 Missing male, Yes Tor area
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 16. Dartmoor SRT Tavistock was called by our sister team from Okehampton at 04:39, to assist them in a search on the north of Dartmoor. A serviceman had not returned from a solo navigation exercise and there were concerns for his welfare. We deployed two search parties from Meldon Dam car park, one to search the Red-a-Ven Brook valley and the other up Longstone Hill and over Okehampton Common to the summit of Yes Tor. Not long after the hill party had arrived at the Tor, two searching military personnel were encountered and as we separated they called to say that the subject of the search had just self-recovered to base and was fit and well. We were stood down and returned to our RVP at Meldon. A very good outcome.

item.title: 4.9.23 Injured female near Warren House Inn
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 17. Our team was called by the Police at 15:03 to assist the Ambulance service with the evacuation of a walker from moorland. She had sustained a painful injury to a knee and could not walk further. She was stretchered to a waiting Ambulance at King's Oven car park.

item.title: 12.9.23 Injured horse rider
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 18. The Team was called at 16:53 to assist in the evacuation of a fallen horse rider with suspected spinal injury. Due to the possible serious nature of the incident members went directly to our Rescue Centre to deploy vehicles while the duty Incident Manager obtained further details regarding the exact location. It was eventually determined that the incident was further south than originally stated, near Harford Moor Gate and so the response was handed to DSRT Plymouth. They were stood down as adequate South West Ambulance Service personnel had arrived on scene.

item.title: 22.9.23 Lost persons north of Two Bridges
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 19. The Police called our Team at 20:41 to respond to an emergency call from three persons lost between Beardown Hill Plantation and Beardown Tors. On arrival at the RVP at Two Bridges a hasty team was deployed by vehicle to Beardown Farm and tasked to search north along Devonport Leat . A search manager sent a team member to the Two Bridges Hotel to check whether anyone had recently returned from the moor, and it was confirmed that the subjects of our search were present and uninjured. The Team was stood down at 21:34.

item.title: 26.9.23 Missing female, Throwleigh
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 20. At 09:13 North Dartmoor Search & Rescue Team called DSRT Tavistock to assist them in a search for a woman deemed to be at high risk who had been missing since the previous evening. They had searched throughout the night to no avail. At 10:40 a helicopter crew of the National Police Air Service spotted the subject near Raybarrow Pool on Throwleigh Common. One search party went to her while a stretcher party deployed from Shilstone Tor. She was assessed as unable to walk off and so was then stretchered back to Shilstone Tor and handed over at 14:10 for further care. On return to our RVP we were greeted by the Rapid Relief Team who provided welcome refreshments for SAR team members, some of whom had been on the moor for over twelve hours. That support was appreciated greatly. A successful outcome from joint working.

item.title: 30.9.23 Missing female walker Ryder's Hill
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 21. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 21:50 on Saturday by DSRT(Ashburton), who'd been tasked to search for a missing walker in the Ryders Hill area.  GPS data received from her 999 call to the Police suggested that the person was near Laughter Tor so Ashburton team deployed to Dunnabridge Pound, and after an unfruitful hasty search of the spot requested our assistance to widen the search area.  Unfortunately the subject's phone battery died, so she was unable to respond to a Sarloc.

We deployed teams from Combestone Tor, where the subject's vehicle was parked, searching south through the low cloud, rain & tussocks as far as Ryders Hill.  With no torch to look for, searchers were reliant on sound, using search horns and listening for a response, which was made very difficult by the wind.  Mindful of the time and the fact we were providing safety support for the Abbots Way Walk on the Sunday morning, our teams were not retasked and DSRT Tavistock stood down at 0300 hours.  Okehampton team arrived to continue the search, alongside Coastguard and Police assets. 

As we arrived at Peat Cot at 09:00 to cover the Abbots Way Walk we learned that the lady had been found at 06:10 hours by Okehampton team members, cold and wet but otherwise OK, and was walked off the moor - a great result.

item.title: 1.10.23 Injured walker near Plym Ford
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: While staffing a checkpoint on the Abbot's Way Walk we were alerted to an incident near Plym Ford, where a male walker had sustained an injury to his foot. One of our hill parties went to the site and administered casualty care and a Team Land Rover was deployed to transport further kit and a stretcher to that location. The casualty was evacuated from the Moor to the road at Peat Cot. A family member collected him for transport to hospital, where it was confirmed that he had sustained a fracture..

item.title: 1st and 2nd November Storm Ciaran
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
All seven Mountain Rescue Teams in the region put their Water team members on alert to assist in response to any incidents caused by Storm Ciaran, as widespread flooding was predicted by the Met Office and Environment Agency. Fortunately for the public overnight there were no incidents requiring our resources.

Incident 22. At 10:15, as the strongest winds and rain were beginning to subside DSRT Tavistock Water Team was called, as well as that of DSRT Plymouth to attend an incident below Lopwell Dam. Multiple agencies were involved in locating and recovering a car submerged in the River Tavy. The female occupant was extracted and taken to Derriford Hospital, where she was declared deceased. Searches of the river banks were carried out to ensure that no-one else was requiring assistance. Members returned to base at 15:00. Our thoughts are with the family at this sad time.

item.title: 15.11.23 Lost and cold female walker.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 23. DSRT Tavistock was called at 12:56 to assist a female walker who was very cold and lost on the Moor. A hill party was deployed from Peat Cot and at 14:30 located the subject and her dog Benji near to Broad Rock. After warming with an extra jacket and hot coffee she was happy to be escorted back to our RVP. We stood down the National Police Air Service helicopter which arrived above and reached the road at Peat Cot at 15:30. Benji and his owner were then transported to their own transport at Norsworthy Bridge, Burrator.

item.title: 10.12.23 Injured Mountain Biker
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 24. Our Team was called by the Police at 17:35 to assist with an incident at Gawton Gravity Hub near Bere Alston. Two hours before we received the call a 16 year old competitor in a downhill cycle race had hit a tree at speed and been catapulted from his bike and down a slope. Our first member was at the casualty site within 20 minutes and confirmed the subject had sustained trauma to his head as well as suspected neck and back injury. He was immobilised in a vacuum mattress and then stretchered through the woods to our RV point. He was monitored and kept warm in the vehicle until handed over to South West Ambulance personnel who arrived at 19:40. We wish the lad a speedy recovery.

item.title: 21.12.23 Assist Ambulance Service with a patient
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 25. DSRT Tavistock was called at 05:54 to assist South West Ambulance Trust personnel in removing an 84 year old male patient from the upper storey of a cottage on the outskirts of Lydford, near the National Trust White Lady Waterfall car park. Due to the narrow staircase a stretcher could not be used, and so team members lowered the gentleman using a vacuum mattress and then transported him down the track to the waiting Ambulance. We wish him a swift recovery.

item.title: 31.12.23 Injured walker near Down Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 26. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 15:55 on New Year's Eve to assist an injured walker near Down Tor, who had slipped off a rock and was unable to walk.  It had been a particularly wet and windy day, and was now getting dark.  A PhoneFind was sent to confirm their location.  

The first team deployed from the RV at 16:20 and started their assessment of the casualty about 10 minutes later.  The casualty's wife and child were escorted back to the RVP whilst a vacuum splint was applied to the casualty's injured knee.  He was then packaged in a vacuum mattress and stretchered to the RV to be taken to A&E at Derriford Hospital.

item.title: 18.1.2024 Missing high Risk Male, Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 1. DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police at 21:10 to search for a 56 year old male who was deemed to be at high risk. He was last seen near Burrator Reservoir at 10:00. Search parties, including a Search Dog team, were deployed in sub-zero temperatures and searched woodland and open moorland until stood down at 01:30. On return to the RVP they were welcomed with hot drinks kindly provided by members of Rapid Relief Team.

item.title: 19.1.2024 Missing high risk Male , Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 2. At 08:59 our team was called by the Police to resume a search of the Burrator area for the subject of our previous search who was believed to still be on the moor in spite of freezing overnight conditions. A multi-agency search began involving our members along with Police, including a dog team and drone team, HM Coastguard and the Urban Search and Rescue team from the Fire Service. Devon & Cornwall 4x4 Response assisted in transportation of personnel. The subject was located in woodland by a DSRT Tavistock team at 12:30, and his condition was assessed. He was then escorted to a team Land Rover and transported to the RVP at Norsworthy Bridge. A successful outcome to a lengthy search incident. Many thanks to Rapid Relief Team for attending once more to provide hot drinks and food to all involved in the search.

item.title: 31.1.2024 Missing 90 year old male, N.Brentor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 3. Our team was called at 14:00 to assist the Police in a search for a missing 90 year old male. He was last seen at his home address in the early morning, not dressed for the current weather.

Two search parties were deployed, but not long after their searching began further information was received which indicated that he may no longer be in the immediate area. Our members were recalled and the Team stood down.

item.title: 1.2.2024 and 2.2.2024 Missing male, Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 4,.5 At 16:23 on Thursday 1st Feb the Police called us to search for a male who had gone missing near Norsworthy Bridge, Burrator at around 09:00. A search by a helicopter from the National Police Air Service had not proved successful. At 19:30 at Burrator reservoir it was agreed that due to weather conditions the use of air-scenting Search Dogs was not likely to be effective in dense woodland, and that human searchers in the same terrain in the dark were likely to fare no better when looking for a subject reluctant to be found. It was agreed to wait until daylight.

Today an early morning search of one plantation was carried out by Search Dog Bonnie and that was followed by a search by a hill party in an adjacent plantation. The subject was located at 11:00, unharmed by his overnight experience. He was escorted back to Norsworthy and handed to the care of the Police.

item.title: 3.2.2024 Collapsed girl near Crazywell Pool.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 6. DSRT Tavistock was called at 15:03 to assist with an incident by Devonport Leat, north of Crazywell Pool. A 13year old girl in a team training for Ten Tors had collapsed and was drifting in and out of consciousness. Evacuation by helicopter was prevented by very low cloud.

We deployed a hasty team to go to the given location to assess the casualty, and soon after a team Land Rover with stretcher and other medical kit was deployed from Norsworthy Bridge, Burrator. Supporting members set off, escorting two South West Ambulance personnel to the site.

Following assessment by a team Doctor the casualty was taken down to the track and transported back to Norsworthy Bridge in our Land Rover. She was transferred to the Ambulance at16:45 for further care. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 12.2.2024 Injured walker, Brat Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 7. The team was called at 1732 hours to assist a lady walker who slipped and injured her lower leg coming down from Brat Tor.  The first team was deployed in a Land Rover, continuing on foot from the bridge.  Other team members followed, ready to take a stretcher and equipment to the site.  

The casualty and her family had managed to walk partway back and was met by our first team not far from the ford at 1816 hours.  After an initial examination by the team's Cas-Carers, she was brought back to the RV in the Land Rover and handed over to the Ambulance HART at 1828 hours. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 22.2.2024 Major Incident, World War II bomb, Keyham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 8. Many of our team spent this morning deployed as part of a large scale multi agency effort to support the evacuation of residents in the Keyham area of Plymouth as part of the ongoing Major Incident declared following the discovery of an unexploded WWII device on Tuesday.

item.title: 23.2.2024 WWII Bomb, Keyham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 9.

As a Mountain Rescue Team, our members are used to serving our community, providing a search and rescue service on Dartmoor and other remote and wilderness areas.

Over the last few days, we had a new, and very different, challenge. It has been an honour to join many other volunteers as well as colleagues from the emergency services, armed forces and local authority and to be part of the community response to one of biggest challenges faced by the City of Plymouth.

Our thanks and respect go the professionals who meticulously planned and executed a successful operation, especially those who put their own lives at risk.

The City and its people should feel truly proud of how they coped with the events of this week. Our team members are proud to have played a part in keeping the community safe.

item.title: 25.02.2024 Collapsed walker near King's Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 10. The team was called at 13.35 to support a SWAST ambulance crew. One member of a group of young people on an organised training walk was suffering from hypothermia and was unable to walk off. The group was located north of King Tor. Team members deployed from Four Winds Car Park and attended with paramedics. The casualty was treated, loaded quickly onto a stretcher and evacuated to a waiting ambulance. Once warmed up, the casualty was discharged to the care of their parents. The weather was challenging today but the group were well prepared and reacted quickly and appropriately. We wish them all well with their ongoing training.

item.title: 2.03.2024 Injured walker, Princetown
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 11. At 20.09 our Team was called by the Police to assist an injured 65 year old walker on the outskirts of the village. The gentleman had fallen into a ditch and sustained an open fracture of a lower leg bone. The first of our members was on scene within 20 minutes and assessed the situation. It was decided that the Ambulance crew and personnel from the Princetown Fire Station who were present would evacuate the casualty using their 4x4 vehicle. Our members were stood down at 20:46. We wish him a speedy recovery.

item.title: 16.3.2024 Unwell walker, NorthEast of Hare Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 12. At 17:12 DSRT Tavistock was called by our sister team, North Dartmoor Search & Rescue Team, to assist them with the evacuation of one member of a team training for Ten Tors, who was suffering from a medical condition and could walk no further. Members from both Teams deployed onto the Moor in deteriorating weather conditions as darkness closed in. Once at the casualty site the subject was examined by a team doctor and then packaged in an insulated casualty bag for evacuation by stretcher. This was carried out over difficult terrain in driving rain and thick mist. The rest of the youngsters were escorted to a LandRover at the head of the Rattlebrook peat railway track and were driven to the Fox and Hounds, arriving at 23:00. The casualty and members of the stretcher party were collected at the same track head and transported by LandRovers back to our RVP, where she was handed over to the care of Ambulance personnel at 00:50 Sunday morning. A successful outcome to a joint-team deployment.

item.title: 16.3.2024 Missing group of teenage walkers, north of Two Bridges.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 13. While our Team was involved in incident 12, the Police called us at 23:27 to search for a group of four teenage lads who were on a training walk across the moor, from Postbridge to Little Mis tor. They had not arrived at their proposed camp site and their last known position was above the weir on the West Dart, north of Wistman's Wood. Members of our Team not already deployed were tasked, with colleagues from our sister team, DSRT Plymouth, to search their planned route as well as those alternatives that may have been taken to avoid crossing the swollen river. Fresh personnel were called in to continue the search at first light, and the missing youngsters were located at 08:00, safe and well. Another happy outcome to a prolonged joint-team effort. DSRT Tavistock would like to express their great appreciation for the complimentary coffee and bacon sandwiches provided by the staff of Two Bridges Hotel as our members finished the overnight search.

item.title: 27.3.2024 Missing Male, Brentor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 14. The Team was called at 16:58 to assist with a search for a high-risk 72 year-old male missing in the Brentor area. 31 members turned out to search in steadily worsening weather through very muddy and slippery terrain, managed from our new Control Vehicle, which performed very well on its first outing. The highest priority areas were cleared quickly and the search widened to include other likely spots fitting the subject's profile.  Heavy snowfall on top of already slippery mud were making conditions treacherous, and poor visibility and darkness were making searching ineffective.  It was agreed that searching in daytime would be better and allow time to gather more information and the search was suspended at 2300 hours.

15. Thurs 28-03-24

We were called at 0825 to resume the search in the Brentor area in daylight.   Some more information about the missing person's walking habits was also obtained.  12 team members were joined by colleagues from DSRT(Plymouth), USAR, the Police Force Support Group, and another aerial search by NPAS.  It was too windy for more drone use, with winds gusting gale force, plus heavy rain, hail and thunder throughout the day.  We were glad of refreshments kindly provided by the Rapid Relief Team.  Apart from a search dog team, DSRT(Tavistock) stood down at 1650 and handed over to DSRT(Plymouth).  

We learned shortly afterwards that the missing person was now confirmed to have left the search area, and the remaining assets stood down at 1730.

item.title: 29.3.2024 Injured Female on Dewerstone Track.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 16. DSRT Tavistock was called by our sister team, DSRT Plymouth, at 13:42 to assist them with the recovery of a 36 year old female who had sustained a head injury while on the Dewerstone track, Shaugh Prior. Some of our members assisted with the stretcher haul until handed over to the South West Ambulance crew in the car park.

item.title: 02.04.2024 Despondent male, Two Bridges area.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 17. The Police called DSRT Tavistock at 15:48 to assist in a search for a despondent male who was believed to be at high risk. One of our Team's Search Dogs was quickly deployed as well as a Hill Party team. Further search parties were then deployed onto the moor in worsening weather conditions of heavy rain and thick mist. The subject of the search was located by the Search Dog Team within 50 minutes of deployment, and sadly they confirmed that he was deceased.

We recalled the majority of our members back to the RV point while a few escorted Police Officers and Ambulance personnel to the casualty location. At 19:45 a stretcher party was sent to recover the deceased from the moor, and the deployment was completed at 21:40. Our thoughts are with the family at this sad time.

Once again we thank the Two Bridges Hotel for providing shelter, warmth and hot refreshments to our members between the two parts of this operation.

item.title: 27.05.2024 Lost walkers, Merrivale Range
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 18. The Police called our Team at 19:00, to assist two walkers on Dartmoor, who were lost in thick mist and poor visibility. They had no torches and were concerned that they would not get off the Moor before darkness. Our members deployed from Holming Beam and located them at 20:15. Following assessment they were escorted back to Holming Beam in heavy rain. Colleagues from D&C 4x4 Response then drove them to their vehicle parked at Willsworthy.

item.title: 05.06.2024 Missing male, near Derriford Hospital
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 19. DSRT Tavistock was called out at 11:31 to assist DSRT(Plymouth) in searching for a missing person near Derriford Hospital, Plymouth.  Search parties comprising members from both teams and MRSDE search dogs searched the wooded and open areas in the nearby nature reserve, whilst the police helicopter operated overhead.  The missing person was found at14:55 .  It was a good example of how seamlessly different teams work together.  

Members returned to work before attending team training in the evening.

item.title: 06.06.2024 Missing Despondent, near Horrabridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 20. Our Team was called at 10:26 to assist the Police with a search for a missing male deemed to be at high risk. The Team members were put on standby while further details were obtained and a search manager deployed. We were stood down soon after, as fortunately the subject had been located unharmed.

item.title: 07.06.2024 Two dog walkers lost in Lydford Forest
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 21. We were called at 1710 hours to search for a pair of dog walkers disoriented in Lydford Forest.  We were unable to contact them by mobile phone as their battery was very low when calling 999.  As the first team members arrived we learned that the Police helicopter had located the pair, so team members accompanied the Police to meet them, followed by Land Rover 53.  The walkers were uninjured and in good spirits and returned to the car park in a team vehicle.  The team was stood down at 1803 hours.

Thanks to North Dartmoor SRT for sending their control vehicle, as ours was at the garage today, in case it turned into a long search.  Thanks also to Devon 4x4 Response for mobilising 2 vehicles so we could transport teams quickly to the bottom of the woods.

item.title: 12.6.2024 missing elderly male in Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 22. Our Team was called by the Police at 02:15 to assist in the search for a missing 93 year old male, who had last been seen in the centre of Tavistock at 14:00 the day before. Team members searched the Meadows, cycle track and river. We stood down at 07:00 awaiting further information from the Police. Sadly the missing person was located, deceased, on private land fairly soon after. Our thoughts are for his friends and family.

item.title: 18.06.2024 Injured male at Doe Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 23. DSRT Tavistock was called by the police at 16:45 to assist SWAST with a casualty who was reported to have fallen and injured his left knee and back. In fact, he had been thrown from his horse and was reporting severe pain in his left leg and pain in his right leg.
We responded with our sister Team, NDSART and located the casualty quickly at Doe Tor. Some of the HART team were escorted there, and took over care of the casualty and administered some much needed pain relief.

Treatment took some time but the stretcher party was able to start evacuation at around 19:30. He was stretchered back to the RV and then had a short wait for a SWASfT ambulance to transport him to Hospital in Exeter. Team vehicles were back at base by 22:00.

We wish the casualty a speedy recovery. It was good to work so well with NDSRT and the HART Team.

item.title: 20.06.2024 Injured teenager at Swelltor Quarry
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 24. Our Team was called by the Police at 20:30 to attend an incident at Swelltor Quarry. A 13 year old had fallen from height onto rocks and sustained several injuries. It took only 35 minutes for our initial response party to reach the casualty and assess his injuries and provide pain relief. Once the support team arrived he was packaged in a vacuum mattress and insulated Casualty Bag. He was then stretchered back to our RVP at the start of the Foggintor track. At 23:10 he was handed over to the care of paramedics from the South West Ambulance Trust HART team to await transfer to hospital.

We wish the young lad a speedy recovery.

item.title: 29.06.2024 Ambulance assist at Foggintor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 25. The Police called our Team at 23:29, asking us to provide assistance to SWAST regarding an incident at Foggintor Quarry. The Ambulance Service had been tasked to a 21 year old male who reportedly required extraction from the quarry. Members deployed in Team Land Rovers along the track and met the group of young men, including the casualty, walking towards the road. A team doctor assessed the casualty, who appeared to have recovered, and assessed him to no longer require an Ambulance. The Ambulance was stood down and we maintained a presence until the Police arrived on scene.

item.title: 02.07.2024 Injured walker at Bellever Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 26. DSRT Tavistock was called by a Search Manager from our sister team in Ashburton to alert us to an incident where a 65 year old female had sustained a fractured ankle. We then received a call from the Police requesting us to assist the Ambulance service in evacuating her from Bellever Tor. The Team was deployed and as members entered Bellever Forest our team was stood down as an Air Ambulance had landed at the site and no further assistance was required.

item.title: 03.07.2024 Collapsed 14year old near Plym Head
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 27. Our Team was called by the Police at 18:36 to assist a young girl who was taking part in a Dof E training expedition. Once confirmed that the location was near Plym Head we passed the task to DSRT Plymouth, as it was in their operational area. They subsequently requested our support as there were in fact two casualties requiring evacuation. As DSRT Tavistock hill parties reached Plym Ford we were stood down, as a helicopter had been able to land and had evacuated the casualties to hospital. The rest of their group was escorted safely from the moor. Thanks to Devon & Cornwall 4x4 Response for once again providing transport support. A successful joint operation.

item.title: 10.07.2024 Missing male near Looe
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 28. In response to a request from East Cornwall SAR team for additional resources, DSRT Tavistock deployed a Search Dog team and navigator. An extensive search for a missing 52 year old male, deemed to be at high risk, had begun on Tuesday and the search area was expanded during the day. The search is to continue on Thursday.

item.title: 14.07.2024 Fallen climber, Foggintor Quarry
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 29. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 15:05 to assist the Ambulance service extract a fallen climber in Foggintor Quarry.  The climber hit the ground after some of his protection came out during a fall, injuring his wrist , spine and pain in his ankles.  As he landed on his feet first, the climber was fortunate not to sustain a head injury.  We highly recommend that helmets are worn when climbing to reduce head injuries in falls and from falling rocks & debris from above.  

The casualty was treated by Air Ambulance medics, whilst we packaged him in a vacuum mattress to protect his spine and evacuated him to the helicopter outside the quarry.  Ropes were used to protect the stretcher as we lowered it down to the path, and then later as we lifted it up over the large rock step by the pond on the way out.  It was great to see how seamlessly the team, Air Ambulance medics & SWAST worked together. 

After collecting kit from the quarry and checking that the other climber could safely recover their remaining gear to safeguard against further incident, the team was stood down at 1655 and made their way to the roadhead.   We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

item.title: 4.08.2024 Injured walker nr East Dart Waterfall
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 30. The Team was called at 18:30 to assist a group of three walkers, one of whom had sustained an ankle injury and was unable to walk. Our initial team of two, including a doctor, reached the site at 19:50 and assessed the casualty. Shortly afterwards the rest of our members arrived with a stretcher and medical kit. Once analgesia had been given and a vacuum splint had been applied the casualty was loaded onto the stretcher and the whole party evacuated back to Postbridge, where the casualty was handed to the care of waiting Ambulance personnel. We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

This type of accident can happen to anyone, and shows the importance of being able to give your accurate location and having adequate equipment. This group had a shelter, appropriate clothing and provisions.

item.title: 06.08.2024 Injured female on Drake's Trail near Horrabridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 31. At 14:00 DSRT Tavistock was called to attend an incident on Drake's Trail near Horrabridge. A female was reported to be having seizures following a fall from a mobility scooter. Our first response members arrived quickly at the casualty site and with a SWAST Paramedic assessed her condition, while other members carried medical kit and a stretcher to the scene. For ease of extraction a South West Ambulance Service vehicle was directed to the Old Station, where she was transferred from our wheeled stretcher to the care of ambulance personnel at 15:25. We wish her a quick recovery from her misadventure.

item.title: 11.08.2024 Collapsed walker, Baggator.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 32. At 19:53 the Police called for assistance following a request from the Ambulance service to attend an incident near Baggator. A 22 year old, who had been walking and camping on Dartmoor for several days was reported to be unwell. On arrival at the site he was found to be dehydrated and lethargic and taking a history revealed he had no water and had not eaten since early in the day. He was sheltered from the wind, then given water and glucose, which seemed to improve his condition fairly quickly. When a SWASfT ambulance arrived he was handed over to the care of the crew and our Team stood down.

item.title: 28.08.2024 Overdue walker north of Postbridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 33. At 16:00 the team was called by the Police who had concerns for a walker who had not returned from a camping trip. The 62 year old had set off from Postbridge with three dogs and although overdue had made no contact with family. Search parties were deployed northwards on either side of the East Dart river and we then received information that although unhurt the walker was exhausted and could not get one of the dogs over the stile over the wall near Broad Down. One of our hill parties then assisted him and then escorted them all back to Postbridge, arriving at 19:30.

item.title: 31.08.2024 Injured male at Swelltor Quarry
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 34. The team was called by the Police at 10:54 to attend to a walker who had fallen at Swelltor Quarry, sustaining injuries to his ankle and wrist and a blow to his head. We were able to get to the incident site within 40 minutes along with paramedics from SWAST who tended the casualty. DSRT Tavistock team members prepared a stretcher, with a single line rope setup for security, to extract the casualty from the quarry and then carry him a short distance for evacuation by Devon Air Ambulance. We were supported by two members of Devon and Cornwall 4x4 Response who assisted with transporting team members to and from the incident site. A successful multi-agency operation.

The casualty was in good spirits and we wish him a speedy recovery.

item.title: 12.09.2024 Missing person, Morwellham Quay
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 35. The team was called at 14:33 to search for a missing person near Morwellham.  Within minutes of the Sarcall message being sent to deploy team members, the Police called back to inform us that the missing person had been found and we were stood down.

item.title: 5.10.2024 Injured Walker, Leather Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 36. We were called at 1330 hours to attend a walker who'd dislocated his ankle by Leather Tor.  We initially planned to deploy the first team and kit to the casualty site by Land Rover but the access point was blocked by parked cars, so members were sent on foot.  Fortunately, the casualty and his friend were well-equipped and  had put on lots of layers to keep warm.  

Team members administered first aid and splinted the ankle before stretchering the casualty to the road.  The casualty was taken to A&E by his friend, and the team departed the RV around 1520.

item.title: 1.11.2024 Walkers stuck in mud, south of Bellever Tor.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 37. DSRT(Tavistock) was called at 17:35 to assist the Devon & Somerset Fire & Rescue Service, who were helping some walkers stuck in mud south of Bellever Tor.  Once on scene we learned that the walkers had been freed from the mud and they only required help with the walk off, so we limited our numbers responding.  The group were making good progress towards DSFRS's all-terrain vehicle, which was able to transport them back to the RV.  When all were safely back we stood down fully, returning to base at 1955.

item.title: 25.11.2024 Lost walker, South of Princetown
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 38. The Police called our team at 18:19 to assist a male walker who was unable to get off the Moor due to boggy ground and darkness. He was at a confirmed location and uninjured, so only a small party was deployed to assist Police personnel who had also deployed. The walker was escorted back to Princetown.

item.title: 11.12.2024 Overdue serviceman near Ditsworthy.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 39. Our sister team from Plymouth called us at 08:00 to assist with a search for an overdue serviceman who had been on a solo night navigation exercise. He had last been seen at Ditsworthy Warren House at 21:30 and had not been located during an overnight search by his colleagues. We had already deployed an air-scenting Search Dog team and a Hill Party before we had news that the subject of the search had been contacted and was out of his exercise area, and located on the road West of Peat Cot. He was unharmed and collected by military transport.

item.title: 14.12.2024 Walkers in difficulty north of Postbridge.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 40. DSRT Tavistock was called by the police at 13.09 to reports of a couple of walkers struggling on boggy ground NW of Postbridge. We contacted them by phone which reassured them. A SARLOC was sent which put their location near Braddon Tor.
Our first team of three deployed at 14.04 followed by other team members as they arrived. The couple were quickly located at 14.37 and escorted back to Postbridge car park, arriving at 15.27 very thankful for our assistance. Team returned to base at 16.00

item.title: 14.12.2024 Injured lady, Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 41. While team members were at a fund-raising collection at Tesco they were requested to assist with an incident in the car park. A lady passenger had fallen from a car while it was still being driven. She was complaining of a sore knee and painful left ankle. She was assessed by our members and medical history taken. They assisted in raising her from the wet surface into a wheelchair and transported her into the warmth of the store. One of our members remained with her until an Ambulance First Responder arrived, followed by an Ambulance at 15:40. We wish her a speedy recovery

item.title: 17.12.2024 Missing 10 year old boy, Morwellham Quay
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 42. The team was called out at 17:04 hours to search for a 10-year old, missing at Morwellham Quay. It was wet, windy and already dark, so we immediately called @DSRT Plymouth and some @MRSDE search dogs teams from the region to assist. The terrain was characterised by steep ground, dense woodland and a river which meant that searching was challenging. Other than a place last seen, (the Visitor Centre), we had little information. Further, the child who was subject of our search used non-verbal communication and was likely to resist being found. We planned a search strategy that set up a containment area to minimise the risk that we pushed him further from the Visitor Centre and into the woods. We would then search the surrounding area slowly to ensure that all potential hiding places could be searched. It looked like it might be a long night but, fortunately, at around 19:15, one of our teams heard a noise and located the child who was stuck in some brambles in the woods near the river, about 1km from the place last seen. We deployed a team to take his Mum to the location to reassure him and then returned them to the car park in a team Land Rover. He was assessed by one of our doctors, cleared to go home and warm up, but recommended to seek a medical check-up the following day. This incident was another successful multi-agency response. Other assets deployed were @ D&C Police officers, @NPAS, @DSF boats, @ HM Coastguard and an @RNLI in-shore lifeboat. A fantastic result for all concerned. We wish the young person a speedy recovery and the friends and family around them, a Merry Christmas.

item.title: 21.12.2024 Body recovery, Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 43. The team was called by the Police at 16:05 hours at the onset of the longest night of the year, which proved to be another wet one with winds gusting gale force. 14 team members and both Land Rovers deployed to recover the body of a deceased person discovered next to woodland near Burrator reservoir, which was stretchered to the road and transferred into the care of the undertakers.  Members also helped remove many bin-bags of rubbish found at the scene. Our condolences to friends and family of the deceased.

item.title: 29.12.2024 Lost walker near Burrator Reservoir
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 44. The team was called at 15:08 by the Police to assist a dog walker who'd become disoriented in the fog.  The 3 closest members were deployed as a foot team to the given location, and a team vehicle sent in case any kit or further support was required.  The team was stood down en route as Police had reached the missing person.

There are many mobile phone apps that will give you your location using GPS satellites, and it's well worth installing one in case you get caught out.  It certainly makes our task easier if we know where you are!  Even better is to learn how to navigate, so that once you know your location you can get yourself to safety - mobile reception is patchy and unreliable on Dartmoor.  Check out #AdventureSmart for more information.

item.title: 3.01.2025 Injured walker near Down Tor Stone Row.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: 2025 Incident 1. At 14:45 DSRT Tavistock was called by the Police to assist an injured walker. A dog had collided at speed with the side of her left leg, resulting in pain in her knee that prevented her walking further. Our initial hill party located her at 15:50 and assessed her condition. At 16:10 she was loaded in an insulated Casualty Bag onto a wheeled stretcher and evacuated to our RVP at Norsworthy Bridge, reaching that location at 16:50. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 14.01.2025 Injured walker above Wistman's Wood
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
2025 Incident 2. DSRT Tavistock was notified at around 14:50 that our Team was required to assist in getting a person with an ankle injury to an Air Ambulance. The RVP was at Two Bridges and we confirmed that the casualty was on the east side of the river. A team deployed from the RV with medical kit and a stretcher for a 3km walk, arriving at the casualty site around 16:00 The casualty was loaded onto our Titan stretcher and at 16:15 was carried to the Devon Air Ambulance which took off at 16:25, taking her to hospital.
The casualty was a 60 year old female, one of two walkers visiting from Oklahoma, USA. Vehicles returned to Rescue Centre at 17:30. We wish the lady a speedy and uneventful recovery.

item.title: 19.01.2025 Cragfast sheep
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 3. A local farmer and the Dartmoor Livestock Protection Society Officer reported that a sheep was seen on Saturday, cragfast above a high drop in a local quarry. As they believed it would either starve or fall from that location DSRT Tavistock was asked to assist. Early on Sunday the situation was reviewed. We do not normally effect animal rescues, but as the site was quite visible to members of the public, to avoid risk to anyone that might try to assist the animal we agreed to attend. Members of our rope rescue team deployed and managed to secure the sheep, which was then lowered safely by rope in a "Dumpy" bag to the floor of the quarry. Members then assisted the farmer in carrying it to transport.

item.title: 27.01.2025 Report of flares, near Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 4. We were put on standby by the Police at 09:01 after a member of the public had reported seeing three orange flares in the Burrator area.  Drivers for our team vehicles were arranged in case of deployment whilst the Police tried to contact the military.  They confirmed at 09:41 that the flares were part of a military training exercise with no threat to life and the team was stood down.

item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 5. Our Team was called at 11:43 to continue a search that North Dartmoor SART had been making for a vulnerable missing person. Searches by foot party members and an air-scenting Search Dog team continued throughout the night until members from DSRT Plymouth and Ashburton Teams relieved us. The missing person was eventually located, safe and well, by a member of the public mid morning Wednesday 5th.
