item.title: 9.02.2025 Ambulance assist for 15 year old with asthma attack.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 6. We were called at 14:00 to assist the Ambulance service with a 15 year old who was experiencing a severe asthma attack near Cramber Tor. Members were alerted and ready to deploy when we were informed that a Devon Air Ambulance was now on scene and our assistance was no longer required. The Team was stood down.

item.title: 9.02.2025 Female stuck in marshy ground.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 7. At 15:16 the Police requested us to assist a person who was stuck in boggy ground North East of Black Tor, near the River Meavy. A small team was sent to assist and guide her to firm ground and then escort her to her car.

item.title: 11.02.2025 Missing high risk male, Gunnislake
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 8. The Team was called at 00:40 on Tuesday morning by the Police, to assist in a search in the Gunnislake area for an 85 year old who had not been seen since 11:15 on Monday morning. Tavistock Team members carried out an extensive search covering footpaths, open spaces, woodland and the banks of the River Tamar, assisted by members of East Cornwall SRT. Our members were stood down around 06:00, with members of DSRT Plymouth being called to continue search operations at daylight. Later that day we were updated with the sad news that he had been located deceased, and had been recovered by a team from DSFRS. We send our condolences to family and friends.

item.title: 29.03.2025 15 year old with hypothermia , Beardown Tors
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 9. Our Team was called at 21:16 to assist a teenager who was part of a walking group who had completed 36km that day. They had set up camp for the night, but the adult escorts called for assistance as they had concerns for her welfare because she was assessed as hypothermic and with low energy level. An initial fast-moving Hill Party was deployed to go to the casualty to make a detailed assessment and took an insulated Casualty bag to provide the subject with extra warmth. A second Hill Party then deployed into the thick mist taking further medical kit and a wheeled stretcher. Having rested and been warmed the casualty was able to walk downhill, escorted by our members, and then transported by a Team Land Rover to the RVP, where she was handed over to Ambulance personnel. We wish her a full, speedy recovery.

item.title: 07.04.2025 Missing child, Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 10. At 21:36 the Police requested our Team to assist in the search for a 10 year old child who had been missing for several hours. There were concerns for welfare, including the young age, light clothing and predicted cold weather overnight. Search parties were deployed to places in the town where young people often meet up. At 22.42 one of our teams, which included a doctor, located the child who was cold but otherwise unharmed. An insulated jacket was loaned and a hot drink given while waiting for Police to arrive on scene, and they then took over care of the young person.

item.title: 26.04.2025 Injured walker near Hare Tor.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 11. Our Team was called at 12:21 to assist an injured walker on open moorland near Hare Tor. The 15 year old, who was part of a group training on the Moor, had slipped and injured her right ankle which had become swollen and could not bear weight. Our first hill party reached the casualty site half an hour after Callout and assessed the injury. Further members and Team Land Rovers then arrived, and following splinting of the injury, the casualty was stretchered to one of our Ambulances and then transported back to our RVP at Willsworthy Car Park. Once there she was handed back to the care of school staff members, to take her to hospital for further assessment. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 27.04.2025 Lost walkers above River Walkham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 12. At 15:01 the Team was called by the Police to assist two walkers who had become disorientated during a walk above the River Walkham. The walkers and their dog had set off from the south side of the river, descended into the valley, crossed a bridge and then ascended a steep hill on the north side of the river. One of them was feeling dizzy and had a pre-existing medical issue, and both were becoming dehydrated in the heat. A small hill party was deployed, and located them fairly quickly on the top of West Down. They were given water and then escorted back to our vehicles. They felt unable to make the lengthy walk back to their car on the opposite side of the valley, and so were taken there in a private vehicle.

Incidents like this can often be avoided by correct preparation, including planning the route, carrying a map, having adequate drink and food and suitable clothing for the conditions and length of walk.

item.title: 18.06.2025 Missing person, near Fowey
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 13. We were called by East Cornwall SRT at 10:28 to assist them in a search that was continuing from yesterday for a person missing in the Fowey area.  Six of our members including a search dog handler deployed to assist, with others due to become available later in the day.  They formed part of a multi-agency response, with members from East & West Cornwall SRTs, DSRT(Plymouth), Police, Coastguard cliff-rescue team and helicopter.

We were notified at 13:20 that the missing person had been located alive and was being assessed by a paramedic team member, so the remaining team was stood down.

item.title: 22.06.2025 Unwell walker, Winney's Down, Nth of Postbridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 14. Our Team was called at 15:27 to assist the Ambulance service with a 71 year old walker on the moor, who was reported to be experiencing severe breathing difficulties and was several kilometres from Postbridge. As our first responders neared the rendezvous point within 30 minutes of the callout we were stood down, as the walker had managed to get there and was being assessed by South West Ambulance personnel.

item.title: 26.06.2025 Injured walker, north of Postbridge.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 15. The team was called at 18.48 by the Police to assist the Ambulance service with an injured female stuck in mud above the East Dart River, north of Hartland Tor. A full team callout was sent, to RV at Postbridge car park. Hill parties were deployed on either side of the river to locate the casualty site and she was soon found on the West side of the river along the old disused leat, which was extremely muddy.
Additional members were deployed along with three HART team personnel to the casualty site with our Titan stretcher and kit required to extract the casualty. First aid and pain relief  was initially administered by one of our Casualty Carers who handed over that role to paramedics on their arrival.
Given the very poor ground conditions it was decided the best extraction route was across the river.
As light was failing the HART team leader put in a call requesting a Coastguard helicopter to assist in the evacuation. The casualty had been stretchered down a steep slope and across the river just as the helicopter arrived overhead. She was then evacuated by the helicopter, with three members of our team and the HART team to assist in her transfer to a waiting SWAST ambulance at Postbridge.
This turned out to be a very challenging extraction but was carried out with our usual professionalism and good inter-agency working.
Team returned to our Rescue Centre at approximately 23.00. We wish the lady a speedy recovery.

item.title: 12.07.2025 Casualty evacuation, Foggintor Quarry
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 16. The team was called out at 15:08 to assist the Ambulance service in extracting an injured walker from Foggintor Quarry.  At that time some of the team were involved in rope rescue training so hastily packed up the kit and deployed directly there in our new Toyota Hilux, giving a lift to an Ambulance Officer for the last section of off-road track.  The Devon Air Ambulance was already on scene and had given pain relief and splinted the injured ankle.  The casualty had initially managed to get themselves up the rock steps at the quarry entrance, so ropes were not needed.  With support from two assistants the casualty was able to hobble to the helicopter from there without need of a stretcher.  The Air Ambulance departed at approximately 1600 hours and the team stood down.

item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 17. At 16:47 our team deployed a second time this afternoon to evacuate an injured walker from the Pipe Track near Cadover Bridge, covering for DSRT(Plymouth) who were already committed supporting the Hope 24 event.  The ambulance crew on scene had already splinted the injured ankle, so we were able to transfer the casualty to the stretcher immediately on arrival and transport her safely along the narrow, uneven path and over the gate to the ambulance waiting in the car park.  

It was a good example of how teams support each other to ensure rescue provision across the region.

item.title: 25.07.2025 Missing person, Woolwell
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 18. At 07:03 DSRT Tavistock was called to provide additional resource to DSRT Plymouth in a search for a high-risk missing person on the north end of Plymouth. Whilst the Search Managers were planning the search strategy a member of the public located the subject of our search in nearby woodland. Our team was then stood down.

item.title: 28.07.2025 High risk missing person, Down Tor area.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 19. The Team was contacted by the Police at 20:59 to assist with a search for a despondent missing person believed to be on Dartmoor. There were various reports of locations, and a sighting by a runner, indicating that they had taken a walking route from Plymouth to Burrator Reservoir and then out onto the open moor in the region of Down Tor. Teams, including a search dog team, were deployed to locate. Other teams were deployed with the intention to surround the area in the hope that this would push the missing person back down to the car park at Norsworthy Bridge.  A team located the missing person shortly after 22:00. They were cold but unharmed and agreed to walk back with our team to Norsworthy Bridge where we handed them over to the Police at 23.15. Our thanks to Devon & Cornwall 4x4 Response who provided two vehicles to allow swift deployment of our hill parties.

item.title: 09.08.2025 Injured Walker, Tavy Cleave
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 20. At 17:21 the team was called at the request of the Ambulance service to extract an injured person from the upper part of Tavy Cleave. Hill parties were deployed from Willsworthy Butts, along the track by Land Rovers to take a stretcher and medical equipment to the casualty site. Rope rescue kit was also taken for security on the steep ground. The casualty was unable to stand or walk without pain and so the leg was splinted, pain relief administered and then the casualty was stretchered by team members to an ambulance at Lane End. The other two walkers were uninjured and able to walk off with the stretcher party. It was a challenging route off and took almost two hours, with the casualty handed over to paramedics at 20:50. Our thanks to Devon & Cornwall 4x4 Response for providing two vehicles for logistical support. We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

item.title: 22.08.2025 Missing walker, Bedford bridge, River Walkham
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 21. The team was called by the police at 17.10 to help locate an 85yr old male dog walker who lives with dementia, who had left Bedford Bridge a couple of hours earlier and failed to return. A National Police Air Service helicopter had already started an aerial search. A full team callout was initiated, with the first search party deployed to search the river bank path towards Gem Bridge. Just after the second search team had been deployed the gentleman’s wife returned to the RVP with her husband and dog. She had driven home and found him there, with no recollection of how he got there.
A good result for what could have been a very long search.

item.title: 24.08.2025 Injured walker, between Bellever Tor and Dunnabridge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 22. The Team was called just after 17.00, to assist a lady who had a problem with her hip and was unable to walk any further. Our phonefind app was used to pinpoint the casualty site, between Bellever Tor and Dunnabridge.
Two team members reached her at18.15, with the stretcher party and full medical kit arriving about 45mins later. The lady was then stretchered back to a waiting Devon & Cornwall 4x4 Response vehicle and transported to her vehicle.
Vehicles returned to base at 20:30.

item.title: 24.08.2025 Missing walker, Devil's Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 23. DSRT Tavistock was called at 23.05 by the Police to search for a 25 year old walker who was several hours overdue for a rendezvous with friends in the middle of the Moor. Initially there was confusion as to whether he was walking to Devils Tor from Fur Tor or from Devil's Tor to Fur Tor. Our Team members were put on standby and discussions were held with our colleagues in North Dartmoor SART. The Police eventually confirmed his intended route and at 02:40 a small hill party was deployed to search that route, while plans were made for deployment at daylight of search teams from DSRT Tavistock, DSRT Plymouth and NDSART.
The initial search party arrived at Fur Tor around 06:00 without locating the subject en route, so at 07:00 a full callout was initiated to carry out the deployments planned during the night. A Coastguard helicopter was tasked to perform a search of the area, and was to then airlift teams from Willsworthy Butts to search specific areas. The Helicopter had just landed to pick up team members when we were informed the missing walker had been located at 09:27 near Beardown Tors and was being escorted to the Police. All Teams were stood down, 10.5 hours after the initial call!

item.title: 5.10.2025 Injured walker, western slope of Ter Hill
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 24. Team members had just finished assisting with safety cover and checkpoint duty for the annual Abbots Way Walk when the Team was called by the Police at 13:28. South West Ambulance Service had requested assistance in dealing with a walker with a fractured leg in a remote location on the western side of Ter Hill. A small hasty party was deployed to the site to assess and stabilise the casualty, whilst others went toward Nun's Cross Farm with full medical kit and stretcher, ready to deploy to Ter Hill. As our hasty party were en route a Devon Air Ambulance was seen landing next to the casualty site. The helicopter airlifted the casualty to hospital and our hasty party continued to the site, to check whether the other two walkers needed any assistance in getting off the Moor. We collected our runners from Whiteworks and returned to our RVP, standing down at 15:15.

item.title: 13.10.2025 Missing walker, Whitchurch Down, Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 25. The Team was called at 18:34 to assist the Police in a search for a 75 year old walker deemed to be at high risk. The missing person had last been seen two hours previously near The Pimple on Whitchurch Down, and had not returned home. As team members were arriving at our Rescue Centre to be deployed in search parties we received the good news that the lady had been found safe and well at Tiddybrook Meadow, so we stood down.

item.title: 25.10.2025 Injured young walker, near Princetown.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 26. The team was called at 21:40 to assist South West Ambulance in the recovery of an injured 12 year old walker who had fallen on exposed moorland near North Hessary Tor. The first of our hill parties provided a shelter for the casualty and once the stretcher party arrived our members and Ambulance personnel packaged her in our vacuum mattress and insulated Casualty bag. She was then stretchered to the waiting Ambulance in Princetown, and transferred into it at 23:10. It was a good example of inter-agency cooperation. We wish her a quick recovery.

item.title: 05.11.2025 Injured walker, near Crazywell Pool
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 27. Our team was called at 13:15 to assist the Ambulance service with an incident near Crazywell Pool. A female walker had fallen and sustained a suspected fracture of her right ankle. Team members were deployed in a Team 4x4 vehicle part of the way up the track from Norsworthy Bridge and then on foot to the casualty site. The casualty was treated by Ambulance personnel and then airlifted to hospital by a Devon Air Ambulance helicopter. Our members were stood down and transported the Paramedics back to their Ambulance at Norsworthy Bridge. We wish the casualty a speedy and uneventful recovery.

item.title: 08.11.2025 - Injured walker near Hexworthy
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
The team was called at 17:50 to assist SWAST with a casualty extraction in the Hexworthy area.

We were provided with an accurate location, details of two walkers, one of whom had fallen into the river and injured her knee.  We were informed she was no longer in the water but was getting cold.

A hill party deployed with two paramedics, getting to the casualty site just after 1900.  The casualty was unable to walk and her companion was particularly cold and needed warming. Two further hill parties deployed with a stretcher.

Access to the casualty site was challenging and the only way out involved a river crossing. River levels were high and so we asked DSRT Ashburton to provide back up with a swift water team in case assistance was needed crossing the river.

Fortunately a suitable and safe crossing point for the stretcher party was located and the casualty was handed over to a waiting land ambulance. Her companion responded well to warming and was able to walk off with the stretcher party.

Thanks to DSRT Ashburton for providing their support and the Devon 4x4 Response for assistance with transport.

The team was stood down by 2200.

item.title: 14.12.2025 - Injured Walker - Cuckoo Rock
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
The team was called at 14.46 to attend to a walker in a rambling party who had sustained a leg injury jumping across a river near Cuckoo Rock (Burrator).

The group, who were well equipped, took appropriate action; with the majority returning to the car park whilst others stayed with the injured person to await assistance.

We are able to make contact with the casualty site and obtain an accurate grid reference.

The first team members deployed with a paramedic from SWAST to assess the casualty. A team carrying splints and a stretcher followed.

The Devon Air Ambulance was able to land near to the casualty site and team members assisted carrying the casualty to the helicopter.

All other party members were escorted safely back to the cars at Norsworthy Bridge.

Two Devon 4x4 drivers attended to assist with transporting team members. We were stood down at 17.24

We understand the casualty sustained a broken leg and we wish them a speedy recovery.

item.title: 15.01.2026 - Evacuation due to UXB - Exmouth
item.dc:creator: tavistocksar
item.content:encoded:
Incident 1 2026. The team was called to attend a major incident in Exmouth due to an unexploded WW2 bomb being dredged up in Exmouth Marina. We were asked to provide responders to assist in the evacuation of a cordon while the bomb was to be moved. Our sister team from Ashburton had been out the previous night evacuating properties in the initial 400 metre cordon, and there was a need to evacuate further properties before any work was carried out to move the device.

Bomb disposal team X-Rayed the device, and ran computer simulations to determine the best course of action. This allowed the cordon to be reduced to 515 metres which significantly reduced the scale of the evacuation.

Once we knew that the bomb was to be moved at 4am on the high tide, we were tasked with sending teams out to evacuate properties up to 600 metres from the Marina. All 4 DRG teams, Exmoor and Cave Rescue were involved along with HM CoastGuard Rescue and Devon and Cornwall 4x4 Response.

We were able to start sending members home around 23:00 with the last team members leaving site at around 00:30 on Friday morning.

The device was successfully towed out to sea at around 04:00 in the morning, and has been detonated.

item.title: 27.01.2026 Storm Chandra
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 2. On the 26th January a meeting of the Region's Search & Rescue Teams was convened by Devon & Cornwall Police, to plan for a response to incidents that might result from the imminent storm. Early on Tuesday some teams deployed assets to the east of Exeter as flooding incidents developed. At 15:15 DSRT Tavistock deployed a Water Team of Swift Water and Flood Rescue Technicians to Fire Service HQ at Clyst St George to relieve the teams that had been operational during the day. The Search and Rescue control cell was closed at 20:00 as water levels had appeared to have stabilised, and DSRT Tavistock was stood down.

Incident 3. As the Water Team was returning home it was tasked to attend a new incident, where two elderly persons were stranded in floodwater. That incident was then resolved by Police and our Team was again stood down, returning to base around 21:30.

item.title: 15.02.2026 Injured walker, Wistman's Wood
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 4.

We received a call from the police at 14:27 to assist the Ambulance Service with the evacuation of a casualty with an ankle injury who was situated on the path just south of Wistman's Wood. We deployed our team members to the site to assess, treat and rescue the casualty. An Ambulance and three HART vehicles were also on route. Our members arrived first and assessed the casualty who had already taken some paracetamol for pain relief. SWAST paramedics arrived soon after and took over casualty care at 15:45. The casualty was placed in a casualty bag for warming, loaded onto the stretcher and returned to the RV at 16:37 where they were transferred into a waiting ambulance. We wish the casualty a smooth recovery.

item.title: 02.03.2026 Lost family, West of Horrabridge.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 5. The Team was called out by the Police at 13:46 to assist with a lost family group of 4 people in the area of Buckland Monachorum. After checking the W3W location, confirming with a Phonefind and speaking to the lost party on the phone, we were able to ascertain that they were quite close to a road but they were unsure how to get back to their car. The party were uninjured and generally fine but a little cold and tired. We deployed three team members to meet the party to offer support and shelter, and called Devon &Cornwall 4x4 Response to provide on road transport for the group. 

The group was loaded into DC4x4's vehicle and after a little bit of driving around, the group's vehicle was located and they were able to drive themselves home. All members and DC4x4 were stood down at 16:52.

item.title: 05.03.2026 Walker stuck in mire, north of Wistman's Wood.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 6. The initial SARCALL came from the Police at 11.03 reporting a person stuck in marshy ground and that the Fire Service had requested our assistance. Her location was given as north of Wistman's Wood near the weir.
On arrival at the RVP at Two Bridges we were informed that fire service personnel had already deployed. Team members followed with a stretcher and medical kit as we understood that the person had a lower leg injury. An Argo Cat ATV from Tavistock Fire Station Station was also deployed and managed to get close to the casualty site and was used to transport the casualty back to Two Bridges. She was then fully assessed by two of our Team medical technicians before being transported to her car in Princetown. It was another successful example of good joint-agency cooperation.
Team vehicles returned to our Rescue Centre at 14.00

item.title: 07.03.2026 Missing male, Lee Moor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 7. At 15:50 we received a call requesting navigators for Search Dog teams which were to assist in a search in the Lee Moor are for a missing male. Team members deployed but were stood down en route, as the subject of the search had been located by Police.

item.title: 13.03.2026 Missing person, Tavistock
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 8.

The team was called today by the Police to search for a missing lady in her 70's in the Tavistock area. She had been seen in the area before being reported missing. Whilst we were getting information from the police to allow us to build a search plan, the lady was found safe and well in the vicinity of her home.

item.title: 16.03.2026 Casualty at Tuckermarsh Quay
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 9. The team was called at 14:26 to assist the South Western Ambulance Service after a woman had fallen into a stream in the Tuckermarsh area. An Ambulance crew was already on scene treating the casualty for a suspected broken ankle. As team members arrived they were deployed to assist at the scene.
At around 15:10 the casualty was packaged in a team stretcher and carefully carried from the stream location up to the waiting ambulance, arriving at approximately 16:00, where she was handed over for onward care.
Dartmoor Search & Rescue Team Plymouth had also been responding to the incident but were stood down while en route as additional personnel were not required.
All team members and vehicles were clear and back at the rescue centre by 16:40.
We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.

item.title: 22.03.2026 Injured walker , near Sittaford Tor.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 10. The Team was called out today at 13:10 to assist South West Ambulance Service Trust with the extraction of a young lady who had been training for Ten Tors. Our casualty was between Sittaford Tor and Fernworthy Forest , an area usually covered by North Dartmoor Search and Rescue Team, but they were already dealing with a casualty near Belstone so we were tasked. We deployed our team to RV at Fernworthy Reservoir, and went from there to reach our casualty. She had been looked after by a doctor who had been nearby, and our team packaged and stretchered the casualty to a waiting ambulance at the edge of Fernworthy Forest. We asked for assistance from Devon and Cornwall 4x4 Response to transport the adult who had been waiting with the casualty back to his vehicle. This was the first deployment of our new Hilux after being fitted out with a new storage area and off-road modifications. The team members were stood down at 15:19 and team vehicles were back in our Rescue Centre at 16:20

item.title: 24.03.2026 Police assist
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 11. We received a call from the Police at 13:37 requesting assistance for two officers responding to a report of suspected unexploded ordnance found on Dartmoor by a member of the public. Due to poor visibility and the remote location, we were called upon as experts in the Dartmoor environment.
We deployed a small team in vehicle 63 to a nearby rendezvous point. While en route, we were stood down at 14:10 after the object was located and confirmed to pose no risk.

item.title: 29.03.2026 Medical assistance, Fur Tor.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 12. The Team received a SARCALL message at 02:04 as South West Ambulance Service was requesting assistance for a lone diabetic male at Fur Tor who was suffering from low blood sugar. A full team callout was initiated to RV at Baggator Gate and a HM Coastguard Rescue helicopter was requested to attend due to the urgency of the incident.
A hasty hill party was deployed toward Fur Tor with a second party readying to take further medical kit and stretcher.
Rescue helicopter 924 arrived at the casualty site at 03:38, assessed the casualty and prepared to evacuate him from the moor. At that time we were alerted to another casualty incident at Wild Tor, and we informed the aircrew of that. They were then tasked to that additional incident by Ambulance Control. Our Control remained at Baggator Gate until the helicopter had lifted from both incident sites with a number of casualties on board. We then stood down and our personnel and vehicles returned to our Rescue Centre at 05:.20. Once again an excellent result from multi-agency cooperation.

item.title: 29.04.2026 UXB Southway, Plymouth
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 13. DSRT Tavistock was put on standby at 20:30 on Wednesday to assist with the evacuation of 1200 homes in the Southway area due to the discovery of a WW2 UXB. At 23:00 the team deployed to an RV near Crownhill in Plymouth and met with DSRT Plymouth, Coastguard Rescue, Fire and Police. Through the night we worked to visit every property within a 400m cordon around the UXB, checking properties were either vacated, or asking people to evacuate when found to be still in their homes. Every visit and occupants' plan of leaving or staying was logged, and the data was assessed to make a plan for the following day. The team finished at 05:30 with all vehicles returned to base, and all members heading home to get as much sleep as possible before either work, or the expected follow up deployment on Thursday. We were recalled early on Thursday to continue the evacuation at 09:00, at a new RV at the TA centre in Derriford. Our team members joined multi-agency teams made up of Mountain Rescue, Coastguard, Fire and Police and set out to revisit properties in the 400m cordon to reduce the number of people still in the high risk area. All empty properties were double checked, the dangers presented by the work being carried out by EOD were explained to those who were choosing to remain at home, and where people wanted to leave but had no transport arrangements were made to transport them to a place of safety. Thursday's pace was slow and thorough, with some emotional moments when residents realised the seriousness of the situation.

All MR teams were stood down at 20:30, following a lengthy deployment, especially for those who had also responded the night before.

item.title: 08.05.2026 Collapsed walker, Barnhill.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 14. The Team was called at 15:25 by South West Ambulance Service to attend a walker who had collapsed on Barnhill. Team members reached the casualty within 20 minutes of being called and assessed him. He was then stretchered to Pork Hill Car Park, where he was transferred to the care of SWAST HART Team personnel. We wish him a speedy recovery. The Team then deployed to Willsworthy Camp to prepare for provision of safety cover for Ten Tors.

item.title: 20.05.2026 Missing Person
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 15. At 19:54, during a training exercise, the Team was called to assist the Police in a search for a person deemed to be at high risk. It was fortunate that the person was not far from where our exercise was taking place, as visibility was rapidly reducing as mist and low cloud moved in. Once spotted a couple of team members escorted Police personnel to the location and the subject was left in their care. We then completed our training exercise .

item.title: 03.06.2026 Missing male, Derriford
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 16. At 17:45 we were contacted by our partner team in Plymouth to assist them in a Police search for a 52 year old male missing from Derriford Hospital and who was believed to be at high risk. Members of both Teams were tasked to search various woodland and overgrown areas and industrial units near the hospital. DSRT Tavistock provided 27 searchers including three air-scenting Search Dog teams. The search was carried out in heavy rain and over very difficult terrain and was temporarily suspended at 22:15. Team vehicles returned to our base at 23:30. The search began again at 10:00 on Thursday morning and continued until 17:00. Following some information from the Thursday search a targeted search by another dog team located the missing man on Friday afternoon, sadly deceased. We send our condolences to the family.

item.title: 14.06.2026 Injured horse rider, Burrator
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 18. We were called today at 12:17 by Police to assist SWAST Paramedics with the extrication of a lady who had fallen from her horse near Burrator reservoir. She had a suspected broken left arm and was unable to stand when we were called. Team members were sent to the casualty site to assess the situation, and a team vehicle was sent close to the casualty site to allow a stretcher to be deployed, along with additional team members to make up a stretcher party. After SWAST Paramedics splinted the arm and administered morphine, the casualty was able to stand, and was escorted back to the waiting ambulance. We wish her a speedy recovery.

item.title: 25.06.2026 Missing male, Looe
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 19. The Team was called by the Police at 09:00 and requested to assist with the continuation of an overnight search which had involved East Cornwall SRT. The subject was a male who was believed to be at high risk. In very hot conditions members of DSRT Tavistock alongside members of DSRT Plymouth were deployed to search wooded areas and fields, while Police checked local roads and lanes. Information received suggested the need for a change of search area, so search parties were recalled to enjoy refreshments kindly provided by the Rapid Relief Team, prior to re-tasking to a different area to the north. At 13:00 as they were returning to Control we were informed that the subject had been located alive, and we were stood down, returning to our Tavistock base at 14:30.

item.title: 02.07.2026 Unwell walker, north of Two Bridges
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 20. We were called at 14:24 to assist the Ambulance Service with a lady who had fallen ill while on a walk, and was having difficulty breathing. Ambulance crew and Air Ambulance had already been dispatched and they wanted us to attend to facilitate a stretcher carry to the Air Ambulance. We had team members on site quickly who walked up to the location of the casualty to assess the situation. The casualty had started to recover and was able to walk to the land Ambulance which was parked at Crockern Cottage. Team members accompanied the casualty and the ambulance crew in case the casualty needed further assistance. Vehicles were back at our Rescue Centre by 16:00.

item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 21. The Team was called at 18:10 to assist South West Ambulance Service to recover a casualty from fields above Horrabridge. A walker had taken a tumble on a rough track and was unable to walk due to an injured ankle. Members were deployed with our wheeled stretcher to the casualty site where SWAST personnel were already in attendance. The casualty was packaged in a vacuum mattress and then stretchered down to the village to be transferred to the waiting Ambulance.

item.title: 14.07.2026 Injured walker, Longaford Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 22. We received a call to assist SWAST at 15:09. They were attending a walker with a lower leg injury near Longaford Tor. The team was deployed in addition to Devon Air Ambulance and HART. On reaching the RV at Two Bridges we were stood down as the helicopter had landed at the casualty site and the crew had been able to load the casualty for evacuation to hospital.

item.title: 19.07.2026 Injured walker, Deancombe
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 23. The Police called our team at 13:23 to assist an injured walker near Burrator Reservoir. The casualty had fallen and sustained a dislocation of her ankle. Team members were deployed to the casualty location and following assessment analgesia was administered and a team Doctor reduced the dislocation. A vacuum splint was applied and the patient was transported by stretcher and rescue vehicle back to the RV at Norsworthy Bridge. She was handed over to the care of South West Ambulance Service Trust personnel at 15:40, for onward transport by Ambulance to Derriford Hospital. We wish her a smooth and uneventful recovery.

item.title: 24.07.2026 Missing walkers, Lynch Tor / Baggator area
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 24. Following a report that two walkers were missing, having been to Lynch Tor and then toward Baggator, the Police tasked our Team to search for them. We were unable to contact the walkers by phone, so assumed they may have descended into the valley and lost mobile reception. A Team vehicle searched local lanes and moorland exit points while a foot search party went into the valley toward Coffin Wood. A Police drone team also conducted an aerial search. Eventually further information gave us a possible location, which members went to and found the walkers camped for an overnight stay and fit and well. The Team was stood down at 19:20.

item.title: 26.07.2026 Fallen youth, Leather Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 25. We were called at 15.11 with a request from SWAST for the team to assist with the evacuation of a 14yr old male who had fallen 5 metres on Leather Tor and suffered injury to his head. Paramedics had reached the scene and assessed the casualty, but had neither sufficient numbers nor equipment to extract him from that location. A full team callout was initiated and our 4x4 vehicles transported our kit and stretchers close to the Tor.
Ropes systems were set up to allow a safe extraction. Firstly a single line system was used to secure the stretcher as it was passed hand over hand up to the the ridge at the top of the tor. A dual line system was then used to lower the stretcher from the tor to clear the boulder field. Team members then stretchered the casualty over a kilometre to the waiting ambulance at the roadside. Casualty arrived at RV at 18.09 and handed over to land ambulance. Once again it was good to work alongside other agencies, SWAST and HART. We wish the young man a speedy recovery.

item.title: 04.08.2026 High risk missing person, Down Tor area.
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 26. The team was requested at 20:30 to search for a lost, cold male, deemed to be at high risk. His last known location was near Down Tor. Our search commenced just as it was getting dark with five search parties deployed from Norsworthy Bridge Car Park to search Eastwards between Newleycombe Lake to the north and the track to Deancombe to the south. The subject of the search was located unharmed on the Deancombe track and escorted back to the RVP, where he was handed over to the care of Police personnel. Members returned to our base by 23:00.

item.title: 06.08.2026 Casualties at Sheepstor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 27. The Team was called at 01:28 to assist South West Ambulance personnel with the extraction of a party of three campers, two of whom were unwell, cold and unable to walk off.

Team members deployed with two stretchers and casualty bags for insulation. All three were handed over to ambulance crews at the roadside and the team was stood down at 3:30 am.”

item.title: 09.08.2026 Fallen Horserider, Yennadon
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 28. We were called at 12:05 to assist South West Ambulance Service with a fallen horse rider on Yennadon Down (above Burrator Reservoir) . The casualty was in considerable discomfort with pain in her back. Whilst not far from the road, the ambulance crew needed our assistance to get the casualty off the moor. She was placed in a vacuum mattress for immobilisation and then stretchered down to the Ambulance. We were able to stand down at 13:10. We wish the casualty a speedy recovery.”

item.title: 18.08.2026 Injured male, Foggintor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 29. The Team was called to assist the Ambulance service with a casualty near Foggintor Quarry. A young man had slipped while scrambling with friends and sustained an injury which limited his ability to walk. A foot team was deployed, followed by a team vehicle. Once located he was examined and then transported back to the waiting Ambulance. He was then taken to Derriford Hospital for further examination. We wish him a speedy recovery.

item.title: 23.08.2026 Fallen Walker near Leather Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 30. We were called today at 12:29 to assist the Ambulance service with a walker who had fallen on some rocks near Leather Tor and injured his hip. Team members headed to the RV and our first team set out to reach the casualty, arriving with them at 13:07. A stretcher team followed, arriving shortly afterwards and the Ambulance crew were taken close to the casualty location in one of our 4x4 vehicles. Our Remote Rescue Medical Technicians worked with the ambulance crew to assess and treat the casualty, who was then loaded onto a stretcher and carried back to the road, where the ambulance was waiting.

Vehicles were returned to the rescue centre at 14:30, with all team members returning to their Sunday afternoon plans! We hope the casualty makes a speedy recovery.

item.title: 16.09.2026 Unwell walker, Beardown Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 31. We were called by the Police at 15:30 to assist a walker who had fallen ill near Beardown Tors. We were unable to contact the casualty directly to confirm his location, so we deployed our team members using the information we had. We assembled at Holming Beam and members set off across the valley towards the tors, with our Hilux 4x4 being taken round to head up the track through Beardown Farm, to ensure any equipment we needed was as close as possible to the Tors.

Members reached the location given, but the casualty was not where expected, so searches around the tors were started to attempt to locate the casualty. Contact with the casualty was then made by phone, and he told us he had made a recovery and walked most of the way back to Beardown Farm with another walker, and was planning on getting a lift to his car.

The casualty had done the right thing in calling for help as soon as he realised he was in trouble, and had also done the right thing by calling the ambulance service back to tell them he was making his way off the moor.

A small team who had not deployed were sent to Beardown Farm by car, to meet the casualty and he was checked over by our team doctor.  He then took a lift with the other walker back to his own car.

Our team was stood down and vehicles returned to our Rescue Centre at 17:00.

item.title: 18.09.2026 Injured male, Great Mis Tor
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 32. We were called at 10:56 to assist the Ambulance service with a man who had fallen near Great Mis tor and dislocated his shoulder. Air Ambulance and a land ambulance were en route, and we were requested to assist with the rescue, so the team was deployed at 11:02 to meet at Four Winds car park.

Initial team members were deployed to meet the Ambulance personnel and gather information on what was needed, and other members boarded our Landrover ready to drive up the track to Great Mis Tor with a stretcher. Air Ambulance personnel reached the casualty first and assessed him, encouraging the casualty to walk down towards the land ambulance. The casualty was given pain relief, and his arm put in a sling by the paramedics on site. He was then transported in our Landrover, to give a smoother ride down the track than the ambulance would provide and driven back to the RV, and passed back into the care of the ambulance service.

Team members were stood down and vehicles were returned to the RC at 12:35.

item.title: 23.09.2026 Unexploded ordnance, Falmouth
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded:
Incident 33. Our team was called, along with all other Mountain Rescue teams in our region, to assist in the evacuation of part of Falmouth due to a WW2 bomb found near the dock area. We were initially called on Monday evening, though the evacuation was postponed to Wednesday. The delay allowed the team examining the bomb time to set a final cordon size and for the police to put some firm plans in place for the arrival of volunteers from Mountain Rescue, Cave Rescue, CoastGuard, and a large number of police officers. The cordon was initially set at 300m, and was potentially going to be set at 1400m, which would have included well over 1000 properties. Thankfully it was reduced to 755m which only included around 300 properties, meaning a much smaller impact on the community.

Members of our team set off at 07:00 on Wednesday for Falmouth, arriving at 09:00 where we registered and enjoyed catering provided by the Rapid Relief Team. We were briefed on the plan that had been put together in the preceding days and deployed at 10:00, with all teams heading out to their designated areas to start the evacuation process. Everybody we met was friendly, and kept in good spirits during the disruption. All teams were back at the staging area at around 13:00, and the police commander in charge confirmed that the bomb had been moved out to sea, and we were stood down. We returned to our Rescue Centre at about 16:00, in plenty of time for the evening's training session!.

item.title: 03.10.2026 Injured Male, Lydford Gorge
item.dc:creator: longyearbye
item.content:encoded: Incident 34. Our team was called at 12:37 to assist in the extraction of a male who had fallen from a tree into the river at the head of Lydford Gorge, sustaining an injury to his ankle. South West Ambulance personnel were already with him and had administered analgesia. Members of our rope cadre set up a rope system to ensure security of the stretcher prior to the casualty being carried up the steep slope. Team members then transferred him to the waiting SWAST Ambulance. It was a successful multi-agency response involving personnel from Devon & Somerset Fire & Rescue Service, South West Ambulance Service Trust, HART, Devon Air Ambulance and ourselves.
